Examples #1-3 use difference, alternating-operation, and odd/even-position methods described in Core Concept/Finding a Number Pattern.
Examples #4 and #9 use a_n=a_1+(n-1)d; #5 uses S_n=n[2a_1+(n-1)d]/2, all in Core Concept/The Formulas You Need.
Example #6 uses a_n=a_1*r^(n-1); #7 uses S_n=a_1(1-r^n)/(1-r); #8 uses S_infinity=a_1/(1-r), introduced in the same Core Concept section.

checked: Terms, sequence, series, d, r, a_1, a_n, n and S_n are defined before formulas use them. Reciprocal is defined as 1/x before harmonic sequences. Converges, diverges, absolute value and S_infinity are explained before infinite-series examples.
Arithmetic terms count equal steps and arithmetic sums use endpoint averages. Geometric terms count multiplications; the finite-sum cancellation is explained.

Harmonic teaching explains reciprocal conversion and conversion back; Fibonacci teaching states and symbolizes addition of the previous two terms. Convergence uses explicit partial sums approaching 2, and pattern teaching gives several checks and a whole-list test.
Geometric-ratio division requires a nonzero prior term; harmonic terms and reciprocal denominators must be nonzero. Finite geometric sums distinguish r=1.

Infinite sums specify nonzero first term, |r|<1 convergence, |r|>=1 divergence, and the all-zero exception. Term counting requires nonzero d and an actual last term; the middle-term shortcut requires an odd count. Pattern teaching warns a short list can fit multiple rules.
